title: Open Problem (asymptotic behavior of f(H,q))
statement_text: Determine or estimate the asymptotic behavior of the best possible bound for $f(H, q)$ such that every $K_f$-minor contains a subdivision of $H$ in which every edge is replaced by a path whose length is divisible by $q$.
context_text: Following the paper, a $K_f$-minor is a graph $G$ whose vertex set can be partitioned into $f$ sets (supernodes), each inducing a connected subgraph, with at least one edge between any two supernodes (equivalently for the questions below, a graph containing $K_f$ as a minor). The length of a path or cycle is its number of edges. The authors prove that for every graph $H$ of maximum degree at most $3$ and every positive integer $q$ there is a finite $f=f(H,q)$ such that every $K_f$-minor contains a subdivision of $H$ in which every edge is replaced by a path of length divisible by $q$. This applies to very sparse graphs, since there are $K_f$-minors of average degree arbitrarily close to $2$ in every subgraph, and to (weakly) expanding graphs, which have large clique minors. The degree condition is necessary (there are $K_f$-minors of maximum degree $3$ in which every path between two degree-$3$ vertices has length divisible by $q$), and residue $0$ cannot be replaced by another residue. The proof makes essentially no attempt to optimise $f(H,q)$; using Ramsey graphs for subdivisions as a seed gives some improvement, but the bound is still huge and surely far from optimal. For cycles the authors get a nearly tight bound $O(q\log q)$ (and $<4q$ for prime $q$).
notes: Stated twice: once after the remark following Theorem 1 ('the problem of determining its asymptotic behavior remains open') and once in the concluding remarks. PDF source — math notation appears clean.

title: Informal Conjecture (linearity of g(q))
statement_text: It seems plausible to believe that the lemma stating that every complete digraph on $\lceil 2q\ln q\rceil$ vertices with edge weights in $\mathbb{Z}_q$ contains a directed cycle of total weight divisible by $q$ is not tight, and that the function $g(q)$ (the smallest $g$ such that every $K_g$-minor contains a cycle of length divisible by $q$) is linear in $q$ for any integer $q$.
context_text: Following the paper, a $K_f$-minor is a graph $G$ whose vertex set can be partitioned into $f$ sets (supernodes), each inducing a connected subgraph, with at least one edge between any two supernodes (equivalently for the questions below, a graph containing $K_f$ as a minor). The length of a path or cycle is its number of edges. The authors prove that for every positive integer $q$ there is $g=g(q)=O(q\log q)$ such that every $K_g$-minor contains a cycle of length divisible by $q$, and that $g(q)<4q$ when $q$ is prime; together with the fact that expanders contain large clique minors, this settles a problem of Friedman and Krivelevich on cycle lengths in expanders. The proof reduces to a zero-sum problem: every complete digraph on $\lceil 2q\ln q\rceil$ vertices whose edges are weighted by elements of $\mathbb{Z}_q$ contains a directed cycle of total weight divisible by $q$ (shown with a random labelling and the union bound), and for prime $q$ already $2q-1$ vertices suffice, which gives the linear bound for primes. Linearity of $g(q)$ for every $q$ is suggested in the concluding remarks.
notes: Expressed via 'It seems plausible to believe'; clearly conjectural but no labelled environment. PDF source — math notation appears clean.
